messages.subject: Shiny server - AWS
parts:
Hi!


I am building a web site in WordPress and I want to create an iframe calling a Shiny.

I saw some tutorials on Internet about how to install shiny server in Amazon web services. But all of them have instructions using Linux. I have never used it and my computer is Windows.

Have I to use a Linux computer or just the Amazon server is in Linux and is possible to do it in Windows? Do I need a specific tutorial?

Sorry about the silly question and thanks in advance.


Regards,

Luis

messages.author: 5ab11db47365dff1
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server - AWS
parts:
Luis,

You'll need Linux.  I'd use the latest Ubuntu 16.04.  There will be an image for it in the list of commonly used images ("Amazon Machine Images") when you launch your EC2 instance.



Here are some tips to get you started.

1. Install R:

sudo apt install r-base

2. Install shiny server using directions here:

https://www.rstudio.com/products/shiny/download-server/

3.  Set up your security zone to allow port 3838 to have open access to the internet in AWS.

4.  Upload your apps and test them

5.  If you need a domain name, I'd install nginx, listen on the domain name, and proxy_pass the requests to shiny.

6.  For an iframe to work, you also may need to do some stuff with CORS, it depends.



It's not impossible and if you plan on working with Linux in the future this would be a reasonable project to gain familiarity with the environment, the package manger (apt for ubuntu), and basic networking with AWS/Linux.


Erik

messages.author: 5ab11db47365dff1
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server - AWS
parts:
Luis--you can do all your development locally. Then you can deploy in one of several ways.

1. You can just manually upload using ssh/sftp.
2. You can use git. I'd recommend this. Create a repo of your local app. Test. Commit changes to master and push to a github repo, which you set as the the remote origin. Then on your server you can run git pull origin master. 

Erik
